concepts.name: Continuous integration idea
concepts.summary: Explain that CI means merging changes often and automatically building and testing each one to catch problems early.

concepts.name: Pipeline stages and jobs
concepts.summary: Describe a pipeline as an ordered series of stages made of jobs, such as build, test and deploy, each passing or failing.

concepts.name: Delivery versus deployment
concepts.summary: Distinguish continuous delivery, where releases are ready to ship on demand, from continuous deployment, where every passing change goes live automatically.

concepts.name: Pipeline triggers
concepts.summary: Recall the events that start a pipeline, such as a push, a pull request, a tag or a schedule.

concepts.name: Build artifacts
concepts.summary: Explain that an artifact is the packaged output of a build, such as a binary or container image, that later stages test and deploy.

concepts.name: Pipeline as code
concepts.summary: Understand that the pipeline is defined in a versioned file kept in the repository alongside the code.

concepts.name: Runners and agents
concepts.summary: Recall that pipeline jobs execute on runners, which are separate machines or containers, not on the developer's laptop.

misconceptions.text: A green pipeline means the software has no bugs.
Continuous delivery and continuous deployment are the same thing.
CI is just a tool you install rather than a practice of merging and verifying changes frequently.

concepts.name: Writing a basic pipeline file
concepts.summary: Write a working pipeline definition with triggers, jobs and steps that checks out code, builds it and runs the tests.

concepts.name: Automated test gating
concepts.summary: Configure the pipeline so failing tests or lint checks stop later stages and block merging.

concepts.name: Storing and passing artifacts
concepts.summary: Publish build outputs and pass them between jobs so the same artifact tested is the one deployed.

concepts.name: Dependency caching
concepts.summary: Cache downloaded dependencies with keys based on lockfiles to speed up runs without stale results.

concepts.name: Pipeline environment variables
concepts.summary: Use variables to configure jobs and keep environment-specific values out of the pipeline logic.

concepts.name: Basic secrets handling
concepts.summary: Store credentials in the CI system's secret store, inject them at runtime and keep them out of the repository and logs.

concepts.name: Reading pipeline logs
concepts.summary: Locate the failing step in a run's logs and reproduce the failure locally to fix it.

misconceptions.text: It is safe to commit secrets to the repository if the repository is private.
Caching always makes builds faster and never causes incorrect results.
Masking a secret in logs makes it impossible to leak.

concepts.name: Build once, deploy many
concepts.summary: Analyse why rebuilding per environment breaks traceability and how immutable, versioned artifacts avoid this.

concepts.name: Pipeline parallelism and matrices
concepts.summary: Run independent jobs in parallel and use matrices to test across versions or platforms while managing total run time.

concepts.name: Test pyramid in pipelines
concepts.summary: Analyse where unit, integration and end-to-end tests belong in the pipeline to balance speed and confidence.

concepts.name: Flaky test handling
concepts.summary: Diagnose intermittent failures and decide to fix, quarantine or retry them without eroding trust in the pipeline.

concepts.name: Containerised build and deploy
concepts.summary: Build a container image in the pipeline, tag it by version or commit and push it to a registry for deployment.

concepts.name: Multi-environment promotion
concepts.summary: Design a pipeline that promotes one built artifact through environments, with per-environment configuration and approvals.

concepts.name: Deployment strategies
concepts.summary: Compare rolling, blue-green and canary deployments in terms of downtime, risk and resource cost, and pick one for a case.

concepts.name: Rollback mechanisms
concepts.summary: Implement rollback by redeploying a previous artifact and decide when rolling forward is better.

misconceptions.text: Rebuilding the code for each environment is fine because it is the same source.
Rollback is always just redeploying the old version, even when database schema changes are involved.
Automatically retrying flaky tests until they pass solves the flakiness.

concepts.name: Short-lived credentials
concepts.summary: Analyse why short-lived, identity-based credentials are safer than long-lived stored keys and how pipelines obtain them.

concepts.name: Pipeline security hardening
concepts.summary: Evaluate pipeline risks such as untrusted pull request code, over-privileged tokens and compromised dependencies, and apply least privilege.

concepts.name: Progressive delivery with feature flags
concepts.summary: Evaluate using feature flags and staged exposure to separate deployment from release and limit blast radius.

concepts.name: Automated release verification
concepts.summary: Judge which health checks and metrics should gate a release and trigger automatic rollback.

concepts.name: Database migration in pipelines
concepts.summary: Analyse how to apply schema changes safely using backward-compatible expand and contract steps.

concepts.name: Pipeline performance optimisation
concepts.summary: Analyse the critical path of a pipeline and cut feedback time through caching, test selection and parallelism.

concepts.name: Artifact provenance and signing
concepts.summary: Evaluate how signing, provenance records and dependency scanning establish trust in what is deployed.

concepts.name: Reusable pipeline templates
concepts.summary: Analyse how to share and version pipeline logic across repositories without hindering team autonomy.

misconceptions.text: Running pipelines only on trusted branches removes the need to worry about pipeline security.
Deploying a feature to production and releasing it to users must be the same event.
A database migration can be rolled back as simply as application code.

concepts.name: Delivery performance metrics
concepts.summary: Evaluate a delivery process using deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and recovery time, and avoid gaming them.

concepts.name: Pipeline architecture design
concepts.summary: Design pipeline architecture for many services and teams, covering monorepo change detection, dependency ordering and shared infrastructure.

concepts.name: GitOps and declarative delivery
concepts.summary: Evaluate pull-based, reconciled deployment from a Git source of truth against push-based pipelines.

concepts.name: Governance and compliance automation
concepts.summary: Create controls such as policy checks, approvals and audit evidence that satisfy compliance without slowing delivery.

concepts.name: Resilient release engineering
concepts.summary: Design release processes that bound blast radius, support multi-region rollout and improve from incident learnings.

concepts.name: CI/CD platform trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate hosted versus self-hosted runners, tooling and cost against security, scale and maintenance needs.

concepts.name: Pipeline reliability engineering
concepts.summary: Evaluate and improve pipeline reliability and observability by treating the delivery system as a product with its own objectives.

misconceptions.text: Maximising deployment frequency alone shows a healthy delivery process.
GitOps is just a CI/CD pipeline with a different name and removes the need for any pipeline.
Strict manual approvals for every release are the best way to guarantee compliance and safety.
